cells.tense: The pattern is being laid down now, and for once you are the one holding the pen.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: Say how something should run, in your own words, once — a plan, a room, a recurring argument — then stop. Don't defend it. Don't watch how it lands.
cells.core:
You can see how the pieces fit before anyone else has the words. Walk into a messy situation and the arrangement is already clear to you, and people settle down when you say it. They can stand inside something you named without being told to stand there.

This week, name one of those arrangements out loud without being asked. Pick the thing that is currently formless and describe how it should run — once, plainly, then silence. You don't have to argue for it. You don't have to check anyone's face. What you have been carrying around in your head becomes something another person can use, and you find out what it costs to hand it over.

cells.tense: Soon, the structure will need to be announced before it is ready, and you can feel that coming.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Hold one heading for three days and stop surveying the rest. Choose it because you want it, not because it adds up — then steer.
cells.core:
Where you build the shape, you have started building it before there is any ground under it. The plan runs two moves deep before the first move has been lived, and you catch yourself arranging things around a structure that does not exist yet. From outside it looks like control. From inside it is likely just how much you can see, and how quickly.

So hold one heading for three days. Not the whole route — one direction, kept long enough to find out whether it was ever yours. You will want to keep the other options open. Leave them open and pick one anyway. Noticing is not what needs fixing here. The surveying is. Three days on a single heading will tell you more than another month of mapping could.

cells.tense: A shape was named once and it still hasn't been said again, so here you stand.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Do one job alongside somebody this week — same task, same hour, no splitting it between you.
cells.core:
The impulse to organize was in you, and the sentence that would start it hasn't been said in a while. You see the arrangement, you could name it, and you don't — so nobody has been expecting it from you lately. That isn't a lost ability. It is a door you walked past and keep looking back at.

Do the work next to somebody instead. Pick one task and do it together, side by side, without handing out parts. Structure comes back when it has something solid to sit on, and a shared hour is solid enough. You don't need to announce anything. Nobody has to hand you the shape. It tends to find you when your hands are already busy with the same thing as someone else's.

cells.tense: The frame is being set every day, and you are calling it just how things happened to go.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Pay back something you owe this week — before anyone asks, no credit taken, no mention of it afterward.
cells.core:
You are already setting the shape of things — who does what, what the order is, what is fair in a room — and the story you tell is that you are just keeping the peace. The calls are being made. You call them obvious. Anyone living inside them would not.

Pay back what you owe, and pay it before anyone asks. No announcement, no credit, nobody watching. That much is the entire job. You are not keeping the peace. You are holding a standard, and it shows clearest in the cases you have decided are too small to count. The cases you judge too small are the ones that have been counting.

attempts.check: The draft's shakiest claim is 'if you claim the shape out loud they'll help you hold it' — the record says things make sense in your presence, not that anyone responds to a declaration. A reader could fairly say the structure is theirs and needs no one's help. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small, observable act that teaches something even if my read of the seat is off. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'structure that serves what it organizes' — cut it; it is package vocabulary and it flatters the mechanism.
